# List — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for the list when rows need one row model with ten layout presets over it. The variants cover the shapes lists take — one-line, two-line, avatar, icon, thumbnail, navigational, selectable, expandable, control and grouped — with compact, medium and expanded densities, and `rows` are data with id, headline and optional supporting, leading and trailing nodes, so a queue, a booking list and a ticket list are one declaration each. `sections` switches to grouped rendering with headers and dividers, and grouped data wins over rows; `renderRow` is the escape hatch for full control of one row's rendering. Selectable rows pair each item with a named checkbox in exactly the single and multi-select pattern the Material 3 lists page describes, expandable panels are sibling rows rather than nested ones so list ownership stays valid, and loading renders skeleton rows plus a polite status region. There is no page prop — pagination is the adapter pair, because the list stays presentational and the host slices — no built-in windowing, and no link handling beyond the row's own: navigational rows navigate while action rows report through row press.

## Native

### Features

Reach for the list when rows need one row model with ten layout presets over it — the native twin under the same contract. The variants cover the shapes lists take — one-line, two-line, avatar, icon, thumbnail, navigational, selectable, expandable, control and grouped — with compact, medium and expanded densities, and `rows` are data with id, headline and optional supporting, leading and trailing nodes, so a queue, a booking list and a ticket list are one declaration each. `sections` switches to grouped rendering with headers and dividers, and grouped data wins over rows; `renderRow` is the escape hatch for full control of one row's rendering. Selectable rows pair each item with a named checkbox, expandable rows report expanded state on their disclosure control, and loading announces through the progress region named by the accessible label. There is no page prop — pagination is the adapter pair, because the list stays presentational and the host slices — and platform haptics stay host-wired on select, expand and press, since Kern takes no native-module dependency and feedback is the host's choice.
